detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

This is **DCP V2 4/4**. It carries each packed microbatch's runtime CP topology through HybridStack layout conversion, Mamba, GDP, GDN/GDN2, MTP, MLA/absorbed MLA, and DSA/indexer consumers. Models can be constructed with CP1 and consume successive CP1/CP2/CP4 microbatches without mutating build-time geometry.

`PackedSeqParams` retains real singleton runtime groups and the matching TP×CP group under sequence parallelism. MCore-only group metadata is filtered at the Transformer Engine API boundary. Headwise mixers validate every scheduler-enabled CP size at construction; chunkwise GDP retains all TP-local heads.

Original change authored by @zhongbozhu in [879f596](https://github.com/zhongbozhu/Megatron-LM/commit/879f5968f26f1cce5d71ccc55b17d2aaf1e5ec4d). This PR follows merged #7045, #7046, and #7047. Source lineage also includes #4226 and #6387.

## Behavior changes, including static CP

- Per-token MTP backward now SUM-reduces main/MTP valid-token counts over the effective CP group before computing the ratio. This fixes partition-dependent gradients for **static CP>1 as well as dynamic CP** when valid-token counts differ across ranks. Empty ranks participate; counts are clamped only after reduction. There is one two-element all-reduce per MTP depth per microbatch, including evaluation.
- Under per-token loss, logged `mtp_N loss` becomes a global token-weighted mean instead of a mean of microbatch means, including under static CP. Packed/masked runs may log different values even when CP1 training gradients are unchanged. Legacy normalized logging retains its existing definition.
- Indexer metrics weight each contribution by its runtime CP size when it represents a partial token sum, then reduce over fixed PP/DP×CP/rematerialization groups. The metric remains a mean per logical sample, independent of microbatch order or build-time CP. Logging uses the scheduled microbatch count. CP1 external callers may continue supplying only PP/DP; real CP additionally requires the caller's fixed `dp_cp` group.
- MTP metric mode can change after a cleaned logging window; mixing `calculate_per_token_loss` modes within a nonempty window is rejected.

Dynamic CP requires per-token loss and variable-length packing. Deterministic mode, CUDA graphs, router z-loss, CSA, DSA-GQA, and DeepSeek-V4 are outside the supported combinations. Mamba does not support chunkwise CP; inference remains CP1. See [the dynamic CP guide](https://github.com/xiaoyao0115/Megatron-LM/blob/dcp-v2-hybrid-model-runtime-cp/docs/user-guide/features/context_parallel.md#dynamic-context-parallelism).

## October 29 dedicated unit-test bucket

Addressed the request to keep the new coverage out of the existing SSM buckets in [`e3165e929`](https://github.com/xiaoyao0115/Megatron-LM/commit/e3165e929d7cc810445f33a6093ac9baed8952e0).

- Added `tests/unit_tests/context_parallel/runtime/**/*.py` as a separate dev/latest unit-test job on **H100 (8 GPUs)** and **GB200 (4 GPUs)**. The 24 runtime regression files now cover SSM, MLA, MTP, indexer logging, packed metadata and replay in this bucket. Existing parent buckets exclude these files automatically.
- Reduced redundant GPU work: removed four dense dynamic-CP parameterizations that always skipped and the Mamba helper-only parity case superseded by full-module parity. Consolidated MLA static controls into three runtime cases, reducing those comparisons from 15 model passes to 9. Existing main static SSM/transformer test matrices and replay contracts are retained.
- Real selector CLI plus `yq`: every runtime file has exactly one bucket owner. H100 and GB200 each collect the same **192 unique cases (189 production + 3 experimental)**. The actual recipe parser produces one PR workload per platform, and both rendered scripts pass shell syntax validation.
- **301 infrastructure/manifest checks passed**. Relocated logging/MTP coverage passed **94 cases on every one of 8 Gloo ranks**. Focused two-GPU checks passed **16 parity/SSM cases**, **13 replay cases**, and **7 MTP/TE cases** per rank. The parity run had one expected four-rank skip; the MTP/TE run had two expected four-rank metadata skips. Four-rank-only replay cases remain collected for CI. Runtime metadata/geometry CPU checks, formatting, undefined-name checks and the strict kernel-determinism coverage gate also passed.

The full new H100/GB200 buckets still require their GPU CI runs; the local checks above do not claim a completed four/eight-GPU matrix.

## October 29 rebase

Rebased onto `main` at `7196f838952b1ae51dca1d1a1a585847f1655a60`; the rebase verification head was `e902bf5db3ac6115990e3d7f9cb0fbd242b9e036`. The 25 commits are signed and signed off, with no merge commits above main.

Conflict resolution preserves main's KDA chunkwise CP, shared keyword-only headwise-CP interface, recomputation and FP32 gate behavior, plus GDP's compact decode output and speculative no-copy path. Three constructor regressions protect KDA chunkwise geometries; GDN/GDN2 production and test callers use the shared headwise-CP keyword consistently. Main's contiguous-CP test partitioning and separate input-gradient tolerances remain intact alongside the runtime-CP parity harness.

Post-rebase validation on the existing two-A6000 development container:
- **37 CPU checks passed**, no skips: head geometry, beta, decode padding and noncontiguous-output protocols.
- **16 GPU cases passed on every rank**, no skips: full Mamba/headwise-GDP/chunkwise-GDP parity, native GDN/GDN2 runtime replay, compact GDP recurrent output, KDA packed/unpacked forward and backward with FP32 gates, and direct GDN/GDN2 kernel-input helpers.
- Black, `uv run isort`, Ruff, Pylint, whitespace and the kernel-determinism coverage gate passed.
- GitHub confirms the published head is mergeable. This targeted rebase verification does not claim a completed new full CI matrix or generated functional goldens.

## October 28 review follow-up

Synced with `main` at `f77f360c9`, retaining GDP's FP32 beta sigmoid and the projection-recompute gate view using runtime geometry. Private GDP helpers require explicit forward-local geometry. Runtime group contracts are validated when packed metadata is constructed, and TP×CP selection owns its sequence-parallel predicate.

Added full Mamba/GDP module parity (including chunkwise GDP through HybridStack), TP2+SP runtime GDN/GDN2 parity, static MLA parameter-gradient controls, static CP2/CP4 MTP regression paths, portable real-TE-frontend tests, and eight-rank indexer logging coverage. BF16 serial-vs-CP parameter comparisons use FP32 reduction and documented rounding tolerance; runtime MLA additionally compares against a genuine static-CP2 module at the original tolerance.

New four-GPU H100/GB200 functional recipes exercise Mamba+GDN+attention+MTP with mock variable-length data: CP1/DP4 and TP2+sequence parallelism with mixed linear/attention layouts. Their measured golden files must be generated on the corresponding CI hardware; none is synthesized from a different GPU or configuration.

## October 28 validation (before rebase)

The October 28 review verification used two RTX A6000 GPUs, PyTorch `2.13.0a0+8145d630e8.nv26.06`, Transformer Engine `2.20.2+6ea2a74`, pinned Mamba source `0048fbf2e7b2f214dcbe703ea3dec2b9647595e1` plus the checked-in C++20 build patch, and FLA 0.5.1.

- Eight-process Gloo: **94 passed on every rank**, zero skips, covering indexer PP/rematerialization reductions and static/runtime MTP normalization and token-weighted logging.
- Two-GPU NCCL: **8 passed on every rank** for targeted MTP embedding, precomputed rolling, and GPT/Hybrid layout coverage.
- Two-GPU NCCL: **6 passed on every rank** for MLA static/runtime CP2 controls across RoPE, YaRN, and fused YaRN.
- Native GDN/GDN2 deterministic replay: **2 passed on every rank**, zero replay-test skips. The separate FLA GDN2 parity attempt hit an external Triton compiler/autotuner SIGSEGV and remains unvalidated locally; TP2×CP2 parity also awaits larger-rank CI.
- Full Mamba/GDP module parity on the final head: **3 passed on every GPU rank**, zero skips, including headwise GDP and chunkwise GDP through HybridStack; outputs, input gradients and all CP-summed parameter gradients match static CP2.
- Real installed TE frontend: **10 passed on every rank**, with the recurrence replaced by MCore's dense reference; this does not claim execution of TE's external recurrence kernel.
- Packed topology/producer contracts: **91 passed on every rank** in the focused two-process check.
- Head-geometry/helper/beta CPU checks: **18 passed**.
- GPU paged-stash marker regressions: **4 passed**, zero skips, including FP8 saved storage and CP1/2/4/1 local token geometries under stream contention.
- Real Mamba+GDN+attention+MTP training: **20/20 iterations completed on both GPUs**, runtime CP1 and CP2 observed on both ranks, finite LM/MTP losses, zero skipped/NaN iterations. Local DP2 overrides use 1024 tokens/rank and aligned mock document lengths because A6000 FlashAttention 2 cannot handle inter-document padding with CP; checked-in four-GPU H100/GB200 recipes retain padded inputs. No hardware-mismatched goldens or throughput claims are inferred from this smoke.
- Both functional configs pass real argument/config validation; the recipe parser expands all four H100/GB200 jobs and their rendered shell syntax validates.

October 28 review head: `f5efbcd25b2725c83d15c6cd636b5e8b5b4f70c4`. A follow-up removes DDP autograd hooks from parity reference models, since those hooks consume and clear `.grad` before the harness's manual CP/SP comparison. The two preceding follow-up heads passed GitHub lint. The final head is tracked by [CI run 40736603550](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40736603550). Full GPU execution requires the protected `test` approval: this account cannot approve it, and [the latest queue pass](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40736618020/job/122986781898) reports `ALLOW_PR_RUN_ALL_TESTS=false` for PRs carrying `Run functional tests`, as well as a full queue. The requested full-test label remains in place. No green GPU matrix or measured new functional goldens are claimed. The historical H100 job `19601784`, its “58 tests” claim, and the October 1 CI result are **not current-head validation** and have been removed from the evidence above. Their exact historical test selection/container revision has not been reconstructed.

The existing `nemotron3_super_release_gb200{,_sm}` files store MTP goldens, but their explicit `METRICS` lists currently validate only LM loss, iteration time, and memory. Those historical MTP values have not been hand-edited; regenerating them faithfully requires the corresponding 64-GPU release configuration/data.

## Contribution process

- [x] Added unit and functional coverage
- [x] Added runtime topology and MTP behavior documentation
- [x] Commits signed and signed off
- [ ] Complete current-head CI and collect the new hardware-specific functional goldens

@@ -38,3 +38,40 @@ CP addresses these tradeoffs. With CP, each GPU computes on part of the sequence
 CP support is included on the GPT code path. Other models that share that path, such as LLaMA, can use CP as well. CP works with TP (tensor model parallelism), PP (pipeline model parallelism), and DP (data parallelism). The total GPU count is TP × CP × PP × DP. CP also works with different attention variants, including MHA, MQA, and GQA, with unidirectional or bidirectional masking.
 
 Enable CP by setting `context_parallel_size=<CP_SIZE>` on the command line. The default `context_parallel_size` is 1, which disables CP. Running with CP requires Megatron Core (>=0.5.0) and Transformer Engine (>=1.1).
+
+## Dynamic context parallelism
+
+Dynamic CP assigns a CP group to each packed microbatch according to its sequence
+lengths. Short sequences can use CP1 while longer sequences share the same DP×CP
+domain at CP2, CP4, and other enabled sizes. The model's build-time group remains
+unchanged. Enable it with `--dynamic-context-parallel --use-varlen-dataset
+--sequence-packing-scheduler default_dynamic_cp --calculate-per-token-loss`, and
+set `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank` to the token capacity of one rank.
+`--min-dynamic-context-parallel-size` sets the smallest group the scheduler may
+select (default 1). The largest selectable group spans the DP×CP domain; there is
+currently no independent maximum-size option.
+
+GPT and Hybrid models propagate the selected groups through packed microbatch
+metadata. Runtime CP is supported by standard attention, MLA and absorbed MLA,
+DSA with the MLA path, Mamba, GDN/GDN2, GDP, hybrid layout conversion, and MTP.
+Sequence parallelism also carries the matching TP×CP group. CSA and DSA-GQA do
+not support dynamic CP; DeepSeek-V4 is not supported.
+
+The following constraints apply:
+
+- Use per-token loss and variable-length packed training data. Dynamic CP does
+  not support deterministic mode, CUDA graphs, or router z-loss.
+- Headwise Mamba, GDP, and GDN/GDN2 require their TP-local head/group geometry
+  to divide **every** CP size the scheduler can select. Construction validates
+  this against the caller's DP×CP group, before a long sequence reaches forward.
+- Mamba does not support chunkwise CP. Chunkwise GDP keeps all TP-local heads,
+  avoids the head-sharding divisibility restriction, and is recommended when
+  dynamic CP would select more ranks than the head geometry supports.
+- Inference uses CP1. These runtime training groups do not enable CP inference.
+
+MTP with `--calculate-per-token-loss` sums the main and MTP valid-token counts
+over the effective CP group before scaling gradients. This also corrects static
+CP>1 runs whose ranks have different valid-token counts; it adds a two-element
+all-reduce per MTP depth per microbatch. Logged `mtp_N loss` is a global
+token-weighted mean, including under static CP, so packed or masked runs may log
+different values from older mean-of-microbatch-means metrics.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Dedicated runtime-CP tests must be scheduled once on both CI GPU platforms."""
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import yaml
+
+from tests.unit_tests import find_test_cases
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+RUNTIME_BUCKET = "tests/unit_tests/context_parallel/runtime/**/*.py"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("platform,gpus", [("h100", 8), ("gb200", 4)])
+def test_runtime_cp_bucket_has_exclusive_ownership(monkeypatch, capsys, platform, gpus):
+    """Exercise real bucket expansion, child exclusions, and GB200 marker filtering."""
+    monkeypatch.chdir(REPO_ROOT)
+    recipe_path = Path(f"tests/test_utils/recipes/{platform}/unit-tests.yaml")
+    recipe = yaml.safe_load(recipe_path.read_text())
+    buckets = [name for product in recipe["products"] for name in product["test_case"]]
+    assert buckets.count(RUNTIME_BUCKET) == 1
+    assert recipe["spec"]["gpus"] == gpus
+    runtime = next(p for p in recipe["products"] if p["test_case"] == [RUNTIME_BUCKET])
+    assert any(
+        "dev" in p["environment"] and "latest" in p["tag"] and "unit-tests" in p["scope"]
+        for p in runtime["products"]
+    )
+    # Keep the selector's actual recipe data while avoiding a yq binary dependency
+    # for this CPU infrastructure test. CI's yq expression reads this same list.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(find_test_cases, "get_test_cases", lambda path: buckets)
+    expected = {
+        str(path) for path in Path("tests/unit_tests/context_parallel/runtime").glob("test_*.py")
+    }
+    assert expected
+    owners = {path: [] for path in expected}
+    for bucket in buckets:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["find_test_cases.py", bucket, platform])
+        find_test_cases.main()
+        ignored = {
+            line.removeprefix("--ignore=")
+            for line in capsys.readouterr().out.splitlines()
+            if line.startswith("--ignore=")
+        }
+        selected = set(find_test_cases.expand_pattern(bucket)) - ignored
+        for path in expected & selected:
+            owners[path].append(bucket)
+    assert all(value == [RUNTIME_BUCKET] for value in owners.values()), owners

+"""Shared packed-token layout helpers for runtime CP replay tests."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def _zigzag_shard(hidden_states, lengths, cp_size, cp_rank):
+    """Slice each packed sequence into its rank's paired front/back CP chunks."""
+    parts = []
+    for sequence in hidden_states.split(lengths):
+        chunks = sequence.chunk(2 * cp_size)
+        parts.extend((chunks[cp_rank], chunks[2 * cp_size - cp_rank - 1]))
+    return torch.cat(parts).contiguous()

+
+"""Replay saved-activation marker propagation as runtime CP token geometry changes."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine as te_ext
+from megatron.core.fusions.fused_bias_geglu import weighted_bias_quick_geglu_impl
+from megatron.core.fusions.fused_bias_swiglu import weighted_bias_swiglu_impl
+from tests.unit_tests.determinism.kernels.harness import (
+    CONTENTION_TOKENS,
+    assert_replays_bit_exact,
+    bytes_equal,
+    run_once,
+    seeded,
+)
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.launch_on_gb200,
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU"),
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    te_ext._te_mark_grouped_tensor is None,
+    reason="Transformer Engine does not provide mark_grouped_tensor",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fp8_input_store", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "activation",
+    [weighted_bias_swiglu_impl, weighted_bias_quick_geglu_impl],
+    ids=["swiglu", "quick_geglu"],
+)
+def test_paged_stash_marker_survives_runtime_token_geometries(activation, fp8_input_store):
+    """Packed microbatch row counts may change; views/casts must keep the stashing marker.
+
+    Exercise the actual fused-activation saved tensor, including FP8 storage and
+    QuickGeGLU's clamp/concatenate path, without changing outputs or input/weight
+    gradients. CP1/2/4/1 local token counts also check that a preceding microbatch
+    cannot mark the next microbatch's unmarked reference.
+    """
+    seeded()
+    width = 1024
+    full_x = torch.randn(
+        CONTENTION_TOKENS, 1, 2 * width, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True
+    )
+    full_weights = torch.rand(
+        CONTENTION_TOKENS, 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True
+    )
+    saved_dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn if fp8_input_store else torch.bfloat16
+    for cp_size in (1, 2, 4, 1):
+        local_tokens = CONTENTION_TOKENS // cp_size
+        inputs = (full_x[:local_tokens], full_weights[:local_tokens])
+
+        def fused(x, weights, marked):
+            if marked:
+                te_ext.mark_grouped_tensor(x)
+            saved_inputs = []
+
+            def pack(tensor):
+                if tensor.shape == (local_tokens, 2 * width):
+                    assert te_ext.is_grouped_tensor_marked(tensor) is marked
+                    assert tensor.dtype == saved_dtype
+                    saved_inputs.append(tensor)
+                return tensor
+
+            with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack, lambda tensor: tensor):
+                output = activation(
+                    x, None, weights, fp8_input_store=fp8_input_store, clamp_value=3.0
+                )
+            assert len(saved_inputs) == 1
+            return output
+
+        reference = run_once(lambda x, weights: fused(x, weights, False), inputs)
+        replay = assert_replays_bit_exact(
+            lambda x, weights: fused(x, weights, True),
+            inputs,
+            replays=3,
+            contention=True,
+            what=f"paged stash CP{cp_size} token geometry, FP8 store={fp8_input_store}",
+        )
+        for expected_tensors, actual_tensors in zip(reference, replay):
+            assert expected_tensors.keys() == actual_tensors.keys()
+            for name in expected_tensors:
+                assert bytes_equal(expected_tensors[name], actual_tensors[name]), name

+"""Packed TP x runtime-CP metadata uses the caller's real parallel grid."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.datasets.data_schedule import get_batch_on_this_rank_for_sequence_packing
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.launch_on_gb200
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("local_cp_size", [1, 2])
+def test_packed_batch_records_matching_real_tp_cp_group(local_cp_size):
+    if Utils.world_size < 4 or Utils.world_size % 4:
+        pytest.skip("TP2 with runtime CP2 requires a world size divisible by four")
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=2,
+        dynamic_context_parallel=True,
+        min_dynamic_context_parallel_size=1,
+    )
+    try:
+        groups = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        data_iterator = None
+        if groups.tp.rank() == 0:
+            tokens = torch.arange(32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+            bounds = torch.tensor([0, 16, 32], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+            data_iterator = iter(
+                [
+                    {
+                        "tokens": tokens,
+                        "labels": tokens + 1,
+                        "position_ids": torch.arange(16, device="cuda").repeat(2),
+                        "loss_mask": torch.ones(32, device="cuda"),
+                        "cu_seqlens": bounds,
+                        "cu_seqlens_padded": bounds,
+                        "max_seqlen": torch.tensor([16], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32),
+                        "local_cp_size": torch.tensor(
+                            [local_cp_size], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+                        ),
+                    }
+                ]
+            )
+        *_, packed, _ = get_batch_on_this_rank_for_sequence_packing(
+            data_iterator,
+            dynamic_cp=True,
+            pg_collection=groups,
+            config=SimpleNamespace(sequence_parallel=True),
+        )
+        assert packed.cp_group is groups.dynamic_cp[local_cp_size]
+        assert packed.tp_cp_group is groups.dynamic_tp_cp[local_cp_size]
+        cp_ranks = set(torch.distributed.get_process_group_ranks(packed.cp_group))
+        tp_ranks = set(torch.distributed.get_process_group_ranks(groups.tp))
+        combined = set(torch.distributed.get_process_group_ranks(packed.tp_cp_group))
+        assert len(combined) == groups.tp.size() * local_cp_size
+        assert cp_ranks <= combined and tp_ranks <= combined
+    finally:
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()

+    owned = []

+    singleton = pair = stripe = None

+    results = []
+    for order in ((1, 2), (2, 1)):
+        DSAIndexerLossLoggingHelper.tracker = {}
+        for cp_size in order:
+            local_loss = (groups.rank + 1) * (1 if cp_size == 1 else 10)
+            if empty_rank and groups.rank == groups.size - 1:

+)
+def test_dynamic_cp_rejects_incompatible_heads_before_parameter_creation(
+    monkeypatch, mixer_module, mixer_cls
+):
+    """A CP1 build must reject CP4 at construction, even if CP2 would fit."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mamba_mixer, "HAVE_MAMBA_SSM", True)

+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gated_delta_product, "check_fla_sequence_packing_support", lambda: (True, "")
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gated_delta_product, "chunk_gated_delta_product", None, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common, "HAVE_FLA", True)
+
+    def no_parameter_creation(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("parameter construction happened before the dynamic CP head check")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mixer_module, "build_module", no_parameter_creation, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common, "build_module", no_parameter_creation)
+    config = TransformerConfig(
+        num_layers=1,
+        hidden_size=32,
+        num_attention_heads=2,
+        mamba_num_heads=2,
+        mamba_head_dim=16,
+        mamba_num_groups=1,

+    )
+    kwargs = dict(
+        config=config,
+        submodules=None,
+        pg_collection=ProcessGroupCollection(tp=_group(1), cp=_group(1), dp_cp=_group(4)),

+    if mixer_cls in (mamba_mixer.MambaMixer, gated_delta_product.GatedDeltaProductMixer):
+        kwargs["d_model"] = config.hidden_size
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"runtime CP size 4.*heads=2"):

+
+    class _CaptureLayer:
+        def __call__(
+            self, hidden_states, input_ids, position_ids, padding_mask, decoder_input, **kwargs
+        ):
+            seen.append((decoder_input.clone(), padding_mask))
+            return hidden_states, input_ids, position_ids, padding_mask, None

+    block = types.SimpleNamespace(

+    lengths = (8, 16)
+    full_embeddings = torch.arange(1, 25, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").view(24, 1, 1)

+            logits.transpose(0, 1).reshape(-1, 5), labels.reshape(-1), reduction="none"
+        ).reshape_as(labels),
+        config=_config(num_layers=num_layers),
+        # Exercise both a CP1-built runtime group override and the static CP path.
+        cp_group=static_group if runtime_metadata else cp_group,
+        packed_seq_params=params,
+    )
+    (result.sum() * 0).backward()
+
+    main_mask = mask
+    if derive_labels:
+        main_mask, _ = mtp.roll_tensor(
+            mask, packed_seq_params=PackedSeqParams(cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens)
+        )
+    num_tokens = main_mask[:, indices].sum()
+    grads = [head.grad, hidden.grad]
+    # Match per-token DDP SUM followed by finalize_model_grads' main-token divisor.
+    for value in [*grads, num_tokens]:
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(value, group=cp_group)
+    return [grad / num_tokens.clamp(min=1) for grad in grads]

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_layers", [1, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("derive_labels", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("runtime_metadata", [False, True])
+def test_cp2_cp4_parameter_gradients_match_cp1(
+    cp_groups, case, num_layers, derive_labels, runtime_metadata
+):
+    """Changing runtime CP size preserves parameter gradients, including empty ranks."""
+    device = torch.cuda.current_device() if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

+    reference = _backward(cp_groups[1], cp_groups[1], mask, input_mask, num_layers, derive_labels)

+            input_mask,

+            runtime_metadata=runtime_metadata,
+        )
+        for expected_grad, actual_grad in zip(reference, actual):
+            assert torch.isfinite(actual_grad).all()

+    MTPLossLoggingHelper.save_metrics_to_tracker(
+        torch.tensor(float(loss)),
+        torch.tensor(1.0 if tokens else 0.0),
+        torch.tensor(float(tokens or 0)),

+    )

+def test_global_token_weighted_loss_and_acceptance(monkeypatch, tracker):
+    group = object()
+    save(2, 1, group)
+    save(36, 9, group)
+    save(0, 0, group)
+    # A remote rank contributes 42 loss over 6 tokens. Means of rank/microbatch
+    # means would differ from the global reference (2 + 36 + 42) / (1 + 9 + 6).
+    remote = iter([42.0, 6.0, 3.0, 6.0])
+
+    def reduce(value, group=None, op=None):
+        assert group is expected_group
+        assert op == torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM
+        value.add_(next(remote))
+
+    expected_group = group
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.distributed, "all_reduce", reduce)

+    MTPLossLoggingHelper.track_mtp_metrics(1 / 3, 1, None, total_loss_dict=losses)

+        assert tracker[key].count_nonzero() == 0

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["mamba", "gdp_headwise", "gdp_chunkwise"])
+def test_runtime_cp_full_mixer_matches_static_cp(variant):
+    """Compare output, input gradient and every CP-summed parameter gradient.
+
+    The chunkwise case calls the full HybridStack so its runtime packed summary
+    metadata is constructed from the selected microbatch group as in training.
+    """
+    if Utils.world_size < 2 or Utils.world_size % 2:
+        pytest.skip("requires a world size divisible by two")
+    if not mamba_mixer.HAVE_MAMBA_SSM:
+        pytest.skip("requires mamba-ssm")
+    if variant != "mamba" and not gated_delta_product.HAVE_FLA:
+        pytest.skip("requires FLA GDP")
+    if variant == "gdp_chunkwise" and not gated_delta_product.HAVE_FLA_GDP_CP:
+        pytest.skip("requires FLA chunkwise GDP")
+
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(dynamic_context_parallel=True)
+    try:

+        groups = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        chunkwise = variant == "gdp_chunkwise"
+        # One-Householder GDP needs eight heads to keep its CP2 projected
+        # convolution view aligned to causal-conv1d's eight-element stride.
+        heads = max(4 if variant == "mamba" else 8, Utils.world_size)
+        config = TransformerConfig(
+            num_layers=1,
+            hidden_size=128,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            mamba_num_heads=heads,
+            mamba_head_dim=64,
+            mamba_num_groups=2,
+            mamba_state_dim=128 if variant == "mamba" else 32,
+            gdp_num_householder=1,
+            params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            bf16=True,
+            use_mamba_mem_eff_path=True,
+            linear_cp_mode="chunkwise" if chunkwise else "headwise",
+            linear_cp_layout="contiguous" if chunkwise else "zigzag",
+            dynamic_context_parallel=True,
+            calculate_per_token_loss=True,
+            max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank=128,
+            hidden_dropout=0.0,
+            attention_dropout=0.0,
+        )
+
+        def build(model_config, model_groups):
+            model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+            if chunkwise:
+                return HybridStack(
+                    model_config,
+                    gdp_stack_spec.submodules,
+                    layer_type_list=["M"],
+                    post_layer_norm=False,
+                    pg_collection=model_groups,
+                ).cuda()
+            spec = hybrid_stack_spec if variant == "mamba" else gdp_stack_spec
+            mixer_spec = spec.submodules.mamba_layer.submodules.mixer
+            return mixer_spec.module(
+                model_config,
+                mixer_spec.submodules,
+                d_model=model_config.hidden_size,
+                layer_number=1,
+                pg_collection=model_groups,
+            ).cuda()
+
+        dynamic = build(config, groups)
+        static_config = replace(
+            config,
+            context_parallel_size=2,
+            dynamic_context_parallel=False,
+            sequence_packing_scheduler=None,
+        )
+        static_groups = copy(groups)
+        static_groups.cp = cp_group
+        static = build(static_config, static_groups)
+        static.load_state_dict(dynamic.state_dict())
+        bounds = torch.tensor([0, 24, 64], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        sequence_ids = torch.tensor([0] * 24 + [1] * 40, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)[None]
+        packed = PackedSeqParams(
+            qkv_format="thd",
+            cu_seqlens_q=bounds,
+            cu_seqlens_kv=bounds,
+            max_seqlen_q=40,
+            max_seqlen_kv=40,
+            seq_idx=sequence_ids,
+        )

+        torch.manual_seed(456 + cp_group.rank())
+        hidden = torch.randn(32, 1, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.05
+        output_gradient = torch.randn_like(hidden) * 0.05
+
+        def run(module, metadata):
+            x = hidden.detach().clone().requires_grad_()
+            output = (
+                module(x, attention_mask=None, packed_seq_params=metadata)
+                if chunkwise
+                else module(x, packed_seq_params=metadata)[0]
+            )
+            output.backward(output_gradient)
+            gradients = {}
+            for name, parameter in module.named_parameters():
+                if parameter.grad is not None:
+                    gradient = parameter.grad.detach().float().clone()
+                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(gradient, group=cp_group)
+                    gradients[name] = gradient
+            return output.detach(), x.grad, gradients

+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[1], expected[1], atol=5e-3, rtol=5e-3)

+            )

+    finally:

+"""Runtime-head selection through the real Transformer Engine GDN frontend."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch

+from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import HAVE_TE_GDN, TEGatedDeltaNetAttention

+

+    not (HAVE_TE_GDN and torch.cuda.is_available()), reason="requires CUDA and TE GDN"
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("packed", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_final_state", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("build_heads", [4, 8])
+def test_te_gdn_runtime_heads_preserve_backend_and_backward(
+    monkeypatch, packed, output_final_state, build_heads
+):
+    """CP1/2/4/2/1 head changes preserve TE validation, cached instances and pending backward."""
+    Utils.initialize_distributed()
+    patch_te_gdn_op(monkeypatch)
+    module = TEGatedDeltaNetAttention(build_heads, qk_head_dim=4, value_head_dim=6, layer_number=1)
+    default_backend = module.te_attention
+    checkpoint_keys = set(module.state_dict())
+    seen = []
+    original_forward = type(default_backend).forward
+
+    def capture_forward(backend, *args, **kwargs):
+        seen.append((backend.num_attention_heads, backend.training, id(backend)))
+        return original_forward(backend, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(type(default_backend), "forward", capture_forward)
+    bounds = torch.tensor([0, 3, 8] if packed else [0, 4, 8], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    batch, sequence = (1, 8) if packed else (2, 4)
+    pending = []
+    for index, heads in enumerate((8, 4, 2, 4, 8)):
+        module.train(index % 3 == 0)
+        inputs = {
+            name: (torch.randn(batch, sequence, heads, dim, device="cuda") * 0.05)
+            .bfloat16()
+            .requires_grad_()
+            for name, dim in (("q", 4), ("k", 4), ("v", 6))
+        }
+        inputs["g"] = torch.full((batch, sequence, heads), -0.1, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+        inputs["beta"] = torch.full(
+            (batch, sequence, heads), 0.2, device="cuda", requires_grad=True
+        )
+        reference_inputs = {
+            name: tensor.detach().clone().requires_grad_() for name, tensor in inputs.items()
+        }
+        output, state = module(
+            **inputs, cu_seqlens=bounds if packed else None, output_final_state=output_final_state
+        )
+        expected, expected_state = torch_te_gdn_op(
+            *(
+                reference_inputs[name].reshape(-1, heads, dim)
+                for name, dim in (("q", 4), ("k", 4), ("v", 6))
+            ),
+            reference_inputs["g"].reshape(-1, heads),
+            reference_inputs["beta"].reshape(-1, heads),
+            bounds,
+            output_final_state=output_final_state,
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False,
+        )
+        expected = expected.reshape(batch, sequence, heads, 6)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        loss, expected_loss = output.float().square().sum(), expected.float().square().sum()
+        if output_final_state:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(state, expected_state, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            loss = loss + state.square().sum()
+            expected_loss = expected_loss + expected_state.square().sum()
+        else:
+            assert state is None
+        pending.append((loss, expected_loss, inputs, reference_inputs))
+        assert module.te_attention is default_backend
+        assert default_backend.num_attention_heads == build_heads
+
+    # Delay every backward until all runtime geometries have been used.
+    for loss, expected_loss, inputs, reference_inputs in pending:
+        loss.backward()
+        expected_loss.backward()
+        for name, tensor in inputs.items():
+            assert tensor.grad is not None, name
+            torch.testing.assert_close(tensor.grad, reference_inputs[name].grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert [heads for heads, _, _ in seen] == [8, 4, 2, 4, 8]
+    assert [training for _, training, _ in seen] == [True, False, False, True, False]
+    assert seen[0][2] == seen[-1][2]
+    assert seen[1][2] == seen[3][2]
+    assert len({identity for _, _, identity in seen}) == 3
+    assert set(module.state_dict()) == checkpoint_keys
+    assert list(module.named_children()) == [("te_attention", default_backend)]
+

+"""Shared GDP selective-recompute construction and gradient references."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.fp8_utils import get_fp8_context
+from megatron.core.models.hybrid.hybrid_layer_specs import gdp_stack_spec
+from megatron.core.packed_seq_params import PackedSeqParams
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from megatron.core.ssm.context_parallel.chunkwise import build_packed_sequence_cp_metadata
+from megatron.core.ssm.gated_delta_product import (
+    HAVE_CUTEDSL_GDP,
+    HAVE_CUTEDSL_GDP_CP,
+    HAVE_EINOPS,
+    HAVE_FLA,
+    HAVE_FLA_GDP_CP,
+    HAVE_MAMBA_SSM,
+    GatedDeltaProductMixer,
+    causal_conv1d_fn,
+)
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed
+from megatron.core.transformer import TransformerConfig
+from megatron.core.utils import is_causal_conv1d_min_version
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+HAVE_GDP_DEPS = (
+    HAVE_MAMBA_SSM
+    and HAVE_EINOPS
+    and (HAVE_FLA or HAVE_CUTEDSL_GDP)
+    and causal_conv1d_fn is not None
+)
+
+# The mixer places several divisibility constraints on these: d_inner = num_heads *
+# head_dim must divide evenly by the group count, and the in_proj output width
+# (d_inner * 4 + num_groups * state_dim * 4 + num_heads * 4 = 2064) must stay a
+# multiple of 16 so the FP8 GEMM is legal.
+HIDDEN_SIZE = 256
+MAMBA_NUM_HEADS = 4
+MAMBA_HEAD_DIM = 64
+MAMBA_NUM_GROUPS = 2
+MAMBA_STATE_DIM = 128
+
+
+def _make_config(recompute_modules, fp8_recipe=None):
+    """Build a GDP config; an empty recompute_modules disables selective recompute."""
+    return TransformerConfig(
+        num_layers=1,
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN_SIZE,
+        num_attention_heads=MAMBA_NUM_HEADS,
+        mamba_num_heads=MAMBA_NUM_HEADS,
+        mamba_head_dim=MAMBA_HEAD_DIM,
+        mamba_num_groups=MAMBA_NUM_GROUPS,
+        mamba_state_dim=MAMBA_STATE_DIM,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        bf16=True,
+        recompute_granularity="selective" if recompute_modules else None,
+        recompute_modules=list(recompute_modules),
+        fp8="hybrid" if fp8_recipe else None,
+        fp8_recipe=fp8_recipe if fp8_recipe else "delayed",
+    )
+
+
+def _build_mixer(config, state_dict=None):
+    """Build a GatedDeltaProductMixer, optionally loading a shared state dict."""
+    pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(
+        required_pgs=['tp', 'cp', 'dp_cp']
+    )
+    mixer = GatedDeltaProductMixer(
+        config,
+        gdp_stack_spec.submodules.mamba_layer.submodules.mixer.submodules,
+        config.hidden_size,
+        layer_number=1,
+        pg_collection=pg_collection,
+    ).cuda()
+    if state_dict is not None:
+        mixer.load_state_dict(state_dict)
+    return mixer
+
+
+def _run(mixer, hidden_states, grads, **forward_kwargs):
+    """Run one forward/backward and collect the output and every gradient."""
+    x = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+    with get_fp8_context(mixer.config):
+        out, _ = mixer(x, **forward_kwargs)
+    out.backward(grads)
+    param_grads = {name: param.grad.clone() for name, param in mixer.named_parameters()}
+    return out.detach().clone(), x.grad.clone(), param_grads
+
+
+def _assert_replay_matches(baseline, recomputed):
+    """Compare a (output, input grad, param grads) triple; every tensor bitwise."""
+    base_out, base_input_grad, base_param_grads = baseline
+    recomp_out, recomp_input_grad, recomp_param_grads = recomputed
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(recomp_out, base_out, rtol=0, atol=0, msg="output drifted")
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        recomp_input_grad, base_input_grad, rtol=0, atol=0, msg="input gradient drifted"
+    )
+    assert set(recomp_param_grads) == set(base_param_grads)
+    for name, base_grad in base_param_grads.items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            recomp_param_grads[name], base_grad, rtol=0, atol=0, msg=f"{name} gradient drifted"
+        )
+
+
+def assert_in_proj_recompute_preserves_norm_gate_view(
+    monkeypatch, recompute_qkv, fp8_recipe, cp_size, runtime_cp_size=None
+):
+    """At MB=1, CP1 and chunkwise CP must discard and restore the norm's saved gate."""
+    effective_cp_size = runtime_cp_size or cp_size
+    if Utils.world_size < effective_cp_size:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires at least {effective_cp_size} distributed ranks")
+    if effective_cp_size > 1:
+        if not is_causal_conv1d_min_version("1.7.0"):
+            pytest.skip("chunkwise CP requires causal-conv1d >= 1.7.0")
+        if not (HAVE_FLA_GDP_CP if HAVE_FLA else HAVE_CUTEDSL_GDP_CP):
+            pytest.skip("the selected GDP backend does not support chunkwise CP")
+    if fp8_recipe == "mxfp8":
+        te = pytest.importorskip("transformer_engine.pytorch")
+        available, reason = te.is_mxfp8_available(return_reason=True)
+        if not available:
+            pytest.skip(reason)
+
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=1,
+        context_parallel_size=cp_size,
+        dynamic_context_parallel=runtime_cp_size is not None,
+    )
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+    try:
+        modules = ["gdp_in_proj"] + (["gdp_qkv"] if recompute_qkv else [])
+        config = _make_config(modules, fp8_recipe=fp8_recipe)
+        config.context_parallel_size = cp_size
+        config.dynamic_context_parallel = runtime_cp_size is not None
+        config.calculate_per_token_loss = runtime_cp_size is not None
+        config.linear_cp_mode = "chunkwise"
+        config.linear_cp_layout = "contiguous"
+        if fp8_recipe:
+            config.fp8 = "e4m3"
+        config.gdp_cutedsl_kernel = not HAVE_FLA
+        # Eight heads align the projection's ba width to MXFP8's 32-element blocks.
+        config.mamba_num_heads = 8
+        baseline = _build_mixer(config)
+        recomputed = _build_mixer(config, state_dict=baseline.state_dict())
+
+        baseline_norm_forward = baseline.norm.forward
+
+        def contiguous_norm_forward(x, z):
+            return baseline_norm_forward(x, z.contiguous())
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(baseline.norm, "forward", contiguous_norm_forward)
+
+        projection_gate_storages = []
+        in_proj_preprocess = recomputed._in_proj_preprocess
+
+        def tracked_in_proj_preprocess(*args, **kwargs):
+            outputs = in_proj_preprocess(*args, **kwargs)
+            projection_gate_storages.append(outputs[0].untyped_storage())
+            return outputs
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(recomputed, "_in_proj_preprocess", tracked_in_proj_preprocess)
+        saved_gates = []
+        expected_gates = []
+
+        def capture_saved_gate(module, inputs, output):
+            z = inputs[1]
+            assert not z.is_contiguous()
+            assert z.stride(-1) == 1
+            assert z.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == projection_gate_storages[0].data_ptr()
+            # Inspect the actual Mamba autograd save, including its internal 2D reshape.
+            saved_gate = output.grad_fn.saved_tensors[-1]
+            assert saved_gate.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == z.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+            saved_gates.append(saved_gate)
+            expected_gates.append(saved_gate.detach().clone())
+
+            def check_restored_gate(grad_outputs):
+                assert len(projection_gate_storages) == 2
+                assert (
+                    saved_gate.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+                    == projection_gate_storages[1].data_ptr()
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(saved_gate, expected_gates[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+            output.grad_fn.register_prehook(check_restored_gate)
+
+        norm_hook = recomputed.norm.register_forward_hook(capture_saved_gate)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn((256, 1, HIDDEN_SIZE), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        grads = torch.randn_like(hidden_states)
+        forward_kwargs = {}
+        if runtime_cp_size is not None:
+            groups = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(required_pgs=["dynamic_cp"])
+            cp_group = groups.dynamic_cp[runtime_cp_size]
+            cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, 256 * runtime_cp_size], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+            packed = PackedSeqParams(
+                qkv_format="thd",
+                cp_group=cp_group,
+                local_cp_size=runtime_cp_size,
+                cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
+                cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
+                total_tokens=256 * runtime_cp_size,
+            )
+            forward_kwargs = dict(
+                packed_seq_params=packed,
+                packed_sequence_cp_metadata=build_packed_sequence_cp_metadata(
+                    packed.seq_idx, cp_group.rank(), runtime_cp_size
+                ),
+            )
+        baseline_result = _run(baseline, hidden_states, grads, **forward_kwargs)
+
+        x = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        with get_fp8_context(recomputed.config):
+            output, _ = recomputed(x, **forward_kwargs)
+        assert len(saved_gates) == len(projection_gate_storages) == 1
+        assert saved_gates[0].untyped_storage().nbytes() == 0
+        assert projection_gate_storages[0].nbytes() == 0
+
+        output.backward(grads)
+        assert len(projection_gate_storages) == 2
+        assert saved_gates[0].untyped_storage().data_ptr() == projection_gate_storages[1].data_ptr()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(saved_gates[0], expected_gates[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+        recomputed_result = (
+            output.detach().clone(),
+            x.grad.clone(),
+            {name: param.grad.clone() for name, param in recomputed.named_parameters()},
+        )
+        _assert_replay_matches(baseline_result, recomputed_result)
+        norm_hook.remove()
+    finally:
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()

+"""Reference recurrence and TE-version adaptation shared by GDN test buckets."""
+
+import importlib
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.ssm.gated_delta_net.gdn import torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule
+
+
+def torch_te_gdn_op(q, k, v, g, beta, cu_seqlens, **kwargs):
+    """Use MCore's reference recurrence behind TE's actual layout and shape validation."""
+    outputs, states = [], []
+    initial_state = kwargs.pop("initial_state", None)
+    bounds = cu_seqlens.tolist()
+    for index, (start, end) in enumerate(zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:])):
+        state = (
+            None if initial_state is None else initial_state[index : index + 1].transpose(-1, -2)
+        )
+        output, final_state = torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+            *(tensor[start:end].unsqueeze(0) for tensor in (q, k, v, g, beta)),
+            initial_state=state,
+            chunk_size=4,
+            **kwargs,
+        )
+        outputs.append(output.squeeze(0))
+        if final_state is not None:
+            states.append(final_state.squeeze(0).transpose(-1, -2))
+    return torch.cat(outputs), torch.stack(states) if states else None
+
+
+def patch_te_gdn_op(monkeypatch):
+    """Replace the external recurrence while retaining the installed TE frontend."""
+    for module_name, hook in (
+        ("base", "_import_linear_attention_op"),
+        ("gdn", "_import_gated_delta_net"),
+    ):
+        try:
+            module = importlib.import_module(
+                f"transformer_engine.pytorch.attention.linear_attention.{module_name}"
+            )
+        except ModuleNotFoundError:
+            continue
+        if hasattr(module, hook):
+            monkeypatch.setattr(module, hook, lambda *args: torch_te_gdn_op)
+            return
+    pytest.skip("installed TE GDN exposes no supported recurrence import hook")

+"""Packed metadata factories shared by attention correctness tests."""
+
+import torch

+def make_test_packed_seq_params(sequence_length=None, cu_seqlens=None):
+    if cu_seqlens is None:
+        assert sequence_length is not None
+        cu_seqlens = [0, 6, 19, 22, sequence_length]

+    packed_seq_params = PackedSeqParams(
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
+        max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen,
+        max_seqlen_kv=max_seqlen,
+        qkv_format='thd',
+    )
+    return packed_seq_params
+
+
+def make_test_packed_seq_params_with_padding(
+    sequence_length=None, cu_seqlens=None, cu_seqlens_padded=None
+):
+    """Create PackedSeqParams with both regular and padded cu_seqlens for testing padded sequences."""
+    if cu_seqlens is None:
+        assert sequence_length is not None
+        cu_seqlens = [
+            0,
+            6,
+            19,
+            22,
+            sequence_length - 8,
+        ]  # Actual sequence lengths (with some padding removed)
+    if cu_seqlens_padded is None:
+        assert sequence_length is not None
+        cu_seqlens_padded = [0, 8, 22, 28, sequence_length]  # Padded sequence lengths
+
+    cu_seqlens = torch.IntTensor(cu_seqlens).cuda()

+    packed_seq_params = PackedSeqParams(
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_q_padded=cu_seqlens_padded,
+        cu_seqlens_kv_padded=cu_seqlens_padded,
+        max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen,
+        max_seqlen_kv=max_seqlen,

+def parameter_gradient_shards(module, cp_group=None, tp_group=None):
+    """Return canonical gradient sections, reducing CP and replicated SP gradients.
+
+    Checkpoint factories describe interleaved Q/K/V projection partitions too,
+    so TP parity does not incorrectly concatenate a whole fused projection.
+    Collect all gradients before checking values to avoid rank-asymmetric exits
+    while peers are still waiting in a parameter collective.
+    """
+    gradients = {}
+    parameters = list(module.named_parameters())
+    present = torch.tensor(
+        [parameter.grad is not None for _, parameter in parameters],
+        device=parameters[0][1].device,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    minimum, maximum = present.clone(), present.clone()
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(minimum, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN)
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(maximum, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX)
+    assert torch.equal(minimum, maximum), "parameter gradient participation differs across ranks"
+    for name, param in module.named_parameters():
+        if param.grad is None:
+            continue
+        gradient = param.grad.detach().float().clone()
+        if cp_group is not None and cp_group.size() > 1:
+            torch.distributed.all_reduce(gradient, group=cp_group)
+        if (
+            tp_group is not None
+            and tp_group.size() > 1
+            and getattr(param, "sequence_parallel", False)
+        ):
+            torch.distributed.all_reduce(gradient, group=tp_group)
+        gradients[name] = gradient
+
+    result = {}
+
+    def collect(value):
+        if isinstance(value, ShardedTensor):
+            result[value.key] = (value.data.detach().clone(), value.global_offset)
+        elif isinstance(value, dict):
+            for child in value.values():
+                collect(child)
+        elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+            for child in value:
+                collect(child)
+
+    for name, value in module.sharded_state_dict().items():
+        if name not in gradients:
+            continue
+        if isinstance(value, ShardedTensorFactory):
+            collect(replace(value, data=gradients[name]).build())
+        elif isinstance(value, ShardedTensor):
+            collect(replace(value, data=gradients[name], dtype=torch.float32))
+    return result
+
+
+def assert_parameter_gradient_shards_close(reference, actual, *, atol, rtol):
+    """Compare each TP partition against the corresponding serial section."""
+    assert reference.keys() == actual.keys()
+    for name, (gradient, offset) in actual.items():
+        baseline, baseline_offset = reference[name]
+        assert not any(baseline_offset), "reference must be unsharded"
+        selection = tuple(slice(start, start + size) for start, size in zip(offset, gradient.shape))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            gradient,
+            baseline[selection],
+            atol=atol,
+            rtol=rtol,
+            msg=lambda msg, param_name=name: f"Mismatch in parameter gradient {param_name}: {msg}",
+        )
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def synchronized_assertions():
+    """Propagate a numerical assertion to every rank before collective teardown."""
+    error = None
+    try:
+        yield
+    except AssertionError as caught:
+        error = caught
+    failed = torch.tensor(int(error is not None), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(failed, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX)
+    if failed.item():
+        if error is not None:
+            raise error
+        raise AssertionError("parallel parity comparison failed on another distributed rank")
+

The new reduction is order-independent, which fixes the 2× you were asked about, but it changes what the number means under exactly the configuration this PR enables. Dynamic CP requires `calculate_per_token_loss`, so under dynamic CP every contribution comes in with `reduce_group=<runtime cp group>` and `avg_group=None`, i.e. each rank's `loss` is the token-sum KL of its own shard. The old code summed those over the CP group and divided by `dp.size()`: with static CP *c* and DP *d* that is Σ L / d, the mean per logical sample. This code skips the CP sum, sums over `dp_cp` and still divides by `dp.size()`. With a CP1-built model on N ranks and a microbatch that runs at CP *c*, that is Σ L / N, while the same data under static CP *c* logs Σ L / (N / c): the logged indexer loss is *c*× too small for every microbatch whose runtime CP exceeds the build-time CP, and the long sequences that need CP are the ones under-weighted. `test_dsa_indexer_logging.py::test_runtime_cp_microbatch_order_does_not_change_logging` pins this: for the CP2 microbatch it expects `contributing_sum / size * 10` (25 for four ranks with local losses 10, 20, 30, 40), where the per-sample mean is 50. We ran it: on four ranks with identical per-rank token-sum losses (r+1) in per-token mode, this code logs 5.0 under a static CP2/DP2 collection and 2.5 under a CP1-built/DP4 collection with a runtime-CP2 microbatch, while the merge-base logs 5.0 in both (a four-rank gloo script; we can attach it). If the per-rank-slot value is what you intend, say so in the docstring and the test name, because it is neither the static-CP metric nor the per-token `lm loss` metric (a token sum divided by a rank count). Otherwise carry the runtime CP size in the weight and divide once by the fixed group:

```suggestion
        # CP topology may change between microbatches. Weight each contribution so that
        # the fixed dp_cp reduction below yields the mean per logical sample: CP-partial
        # sums (reduce_group) count once per runtime CP rank, CP means (avg_group) once.
        contribution_scale = float(reduce_group.size()) if reduce_group is not None else 1.0
        tracker["values"][layer_number - 1].add_(loss.detach(), alpha=contribution_scale)
```

with `contributing_ranks = dp_cp_group.size()` (times `gtp_remat.size()`) in `reduce_loss_in_tracker`; this reproduces the static values (Σ L·c / (c·d) and Σ L / (c·d)) and gives the per-sample mean under dynamic CP. A per-token metric (Σ L / Σ tokens, like `lm loss`) is the other consistent choice. Either way the expected values in the test change.

inline_comments.body: With static CP the head counts were checked once, at construction. Under dynamic CP the model is built with the static group (usually CP1), so nothing is checked, and the runtime group size is picked per microbatch by the packing scheduler from the sequence lengths and `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank`, from every power of two between `min_dynamic_context_parallel_size` and the DP×CP size — there is no maximum. The assertion here (and its twin in `mamba_context_parallel.py:118`, and GDN's `_get_feat_dim_split` / `_build_head_perm_for_split_sections`, which do not even assert) therefore fires inside the forward, on the ranks of the first CP group that needs the incompatible size, with a message written for static CP; the other DP groups continue to their next collective and wait for ranks that are gone until the NCCL watchdog. On CPU a `MambaContextParallel` or `GDPContextParallel` built on CP1 with 2 TP-local heads accepts `for_context_parallel_group(CP2)` and raises `nheads must be evenly divisible by tp_size * cp_size` for CP4; GDN with 2 key heads passes the permutation check at CP4 (0 key heads per rank) and dies later in `torch.split`. A Nemotron-H-style 64 Mamba heads at TP8 is 8 heads per rank; with DP×CP = 64 the scheduler is free to pick CP16/32/64 for one long document, hours into a run. We reproduced it on a GB200 tray: a Mamba hybrid with 2 heads per rank, built at CP1 with DP4 and `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank 1024`, constructs fine and dies 48 s in, at the first microbatch the scheduler assigns to CP4, with `nheads must be evenly divisible by tp_size * cp_size` raised inside `forward_step` on every rank — 0 iterations; a GDN hybrid with 2 key heads dies the same way with `split_sections (64, 64, 64, 64, 2, 2) must be divisible by cp_size 4`. With DP×CP = 4 all ranks are in the one CP4 group, so torchrun tears the job down; with more DP groups in the same step the other groups would be sitting in a collective, which is the hang we measured on #7047 (not re-measured here, it needs two trays). There is no config-time guard anywhere: `transformer_config.py:1964` checks the head counts against the *static* CP only, and the two `dynamic_context_parallel` blocks check CUDA graphs, per-token loss and z-loss. Two ways to close it, both fine: validate at construction of `MambaMixer`, headwise `GatedDeltaProductMixer` and `_GDNBase`, when `config.dynamic_context_parallel`, that `nheads_local_tp` / `ngroups_local_tp` / the GDN split sections divide every enabled dynamic group size (`get_valid_dynamic_context_parallel_group_sizes(dp_cp_size)` filtered by the minimum); or add a `max_dynamic_context_parallel_size` that both the scheduler and this check honour. Either way, please make the runtime message name the runtime CP size, and mention in the docs that chunkwise GDP keeps all heads and is the safe choice under dynamic CP.

Keeping the per-head-count variants in a plain dict is the right call: at the TE this repo pins, `GatedDeltaNetAttention` holds no `nn.Parameter` and registers no buffer, stores `layer_number` without reading it, touches no global state outside FP8 (which its forward refuses), and its only tensor is a dense `cu_seqlens` cache created on the input's device — so a second instance per runtime head count is legal and nothing needs `.to()`. That is exactly the property a future TE release could break by adding one buffer, and the adapters would then sit on the wrong device with `.train()` as the only thing synchronised. A one-line guard here keeps the assumption honest:

```suggestion
    def _make_te_attention(self, num_attention_heads: int) -> torch.nn.Module:
        """Build a TE adapter whose head geometry remains fixed across forwards."""
        assert _TE_LINEAR_ATTENTION is not None
        attention = _TE_LINEAR_ATTENTION(
            num_attention_heads=num_attention_heads,
            kv_channels=(self.qk_head_dim, self.value_head_dim),
            qkv_format="bshd",
            layer_number=self.layer_number,
        )
        assert not any(True for _ in attention.parameters()) and not any(
            True for _ in attention.buffers()
        ), "TE GDN runtime variants are cached outside module registration and must be stateless"
        return attention
```

Both reference and parallel constructions now use `wrap_with_ddp=False`; the static-CP2→runtime-CP2 GDN sequence passes in one pytest process after this correction.

Current local results: the sequential static/runtime GDN checks pass after removing DDP hooks; both native GDN/GDN2 deterministic replay tests pass. The FLA GDN2 parity attempt hit a SIGSEGV inside external Triton compilation/autotuning before a parity comparison, so that path remains explicitly unvalidated pending the native CI environment. reviews.body: I found four places where the runtime CP handling still looks incomplete. I've left the details inline.

This PR finishes what the series promised: every hybrid-model consumer that still read the build-time CP group or head geometry (the hybrid stack's layout manager, the Mamba, GDP, GDN and GDN2 mixers, MLA, absorbed MLA, DSA and its indexer, and MTP's rolling, layout conversion and loss normalisation) now resolves the microbatch's runtime group from `PackedSeqParams` through forward-local views that never mutate the module, the static path is measurably unchanged, the MTP per-token normalisation is now provably invariant to how a microbatch is split across CP ranks, and the four concerns raised inline earlier are each closed with a regression test. We ran it on a GB200 tray: the three `pretrain_hybrid.py` Mamba commands that crashed and hung on #7047 train 20 iterations under dynamic CP, and so do a GDN+attention+MTP hybrid, a GDP chunkwise hybrid and a TP2+sequence-parallel mixed-layout hybrid, all within the loss noise between the static partitions themselves; the static path is bit-identical to `main` at CP1, CP2 and for MLA.

Two things come first. The branch has to be rebased: it conflicts with `main` in `gated_delta_product.py`, `main`'s new `test_gdp_beta_sigmoid.py` fails on this tree, and the `keep_gate_view` condition `main` added must move onto the runtime geometry when the conflict is resolved (our resolution passes `main`'s GDP tests on both our machines; patch offered in the comment). And the PR's own dynamic-CP parity tests fail on the 4-GPU configuration the description reports as validated: the new MLA build-CP1/runtime-CP2 cases fail deterministically on the CP-reduced `linear_proj.weight` gradient on GB200 and A6000 alike (12 % of the elements, 0.25 absolute against 0.005 allowed, no static-CP control in the test), the GDN/GDN2 cases fail at 4 ranks by one bf16 step and pass at 2 and 8 ranks and at a 2e-2 tolerance, and two other new tests cannot pass on this head at all, so the reported 58-test run predates the rebase.

Then: the indexer-loss logger's new fixed-group reduction normalises by the static DP size, so a microbatch running at CP2 logs half of what the same data logs under static CP2 and the new unit test pins that value; head-parallel SSM geometry is never checked at construction against the runtime CP sizes the scheduler may select, so a long document aborts one CP group mid-training (reproduced for Mamba and GDN); nothing in the tree or in CI exercises a hybrid model under dynamic CP; and two numerics changes reach users who never enable dynamic CP (the MTP gradient normalisation at static CP > 1, a genuine fix, and the token-weighted `mtp_N loss` under per-token loss, which two release goldens pin exactly) and should be stated as such. Two questions would help: which tests and container job 19601784 ran and whether it covers the commits after the October 1 refresh, and which hybrid configuration has trained under dynamic CP on this branch. If #7143 to #7146 are superseded by this series, closing them when this merges would help the next reader.

Concretely, before the next round: please sync the branch with `main` (resolving the `gated_delta_product.py` conflict as above) and trigger CI on the synced head. The head we reviewed has only the DCO and approval checks, so none of the unit or functional tests have run on it, and the parity failures above are easiest to settle on a CI run we can all read.

Notes on lines outside the diff:

- The unit tests pin the individual mechanisms well, but the integration that broke in #7047 — `pretrain_hybrid.py` with Mamba or GDN layers receiving a microbatch whose runtime group differs from the build-time group — is still not exercised anywhere automatic: there is no functional recipe (the only packed/dynamic one is `gpt/gpt_packed_train_eval`, GPT only), the CI run quoted in the description targeted an older head and only lint ran, and on `68033c085` only `DCO` and `check-approval` have run. The 58-test 4×H100 job is self-reported on a development container. Credit where due: we re-ran the three `pretrain_hybrid.py --hybrid-layer-pattern M*-M*-` commands that crashed in `causal_conv1d` and hung on the #7047 head (CP1-built DP4 with runtime CP {1,2,4}; CP2-built DP2 with mixed layouts; CP2-built DP2 both zigzag) on a GB200 tray: all six runs (three dynamic, three static references) train 20/20 iterations with no error on any rank, and the dynamic runs agree with their static references to 3.3e-3–4.4e-3 relative in `lm loss`, inside the noise between the static partitions themselves (static CP1 vs static CP2 differ by 5.0e-3 on this tiny bf16 model). The GDN+attention+MTP hybrid (CP1-built DP4, runtime CP {1,2}) and the GDP chunkwise hybrid train 20/20 the same way, with losses in the same band as the Mamba runs, so the end-to-end claim of the series holds for all three mixer families on our hardware. (For the record, not as a finding: those runs trained with the same peak memory as static CP2 and a steady-state iteration time within 7–14 % of static CP2 on this 4-layer h256 configuration at GBS 16, one run each; the gap matches the ~20 % extra, less-filled 2048-token microbatches the dynamic scheduler produces at this size rather than the runtime-CP code; nothing realistic in size was measured, and a production throughput number from you would strengthen the PR.) The TP2 + sequence-parallel mixed-layout variant trains too (20/20, within 1.1e-3 of its static reference). What is still missing is anything automatic: no functional recipe, and no unit or functional CI on `68033c085` at either of our checks. And five tests this PR adds fail on a 4-GPU tray — two by construction (see the comments on `test_ssm_kernels.py` and `test_multi_token_prediction.py`), three on CP-reduced parameter gradients (the comments on `test_multi_latent_attention.py` and `test_gated_delta_net_parallel.py`) — so the "58 tests passed on every rank" result does not describe the current head. Please add a functional recipe (hybrid pattern with M, GDN and attention layers plus MTP, build CP1/DP4, `--dynamic-context-parallel --min-dynamic-context-parallel-size 1 --calculate-per-token-loss`, mock varlen data) with golden values, a second one with TP2 + sequence parallelism so the runtime TP×CP path runs, and let the GitHub CI matrix run on the current head before merging.
- `megatron/training/training.py` line 3874: `training_log` receives the scheduled microbatch count and uses it for the MoE and MTP scales a few lines above, but the indexer scale here still uses the nominal `get_num_microbatches()`. The rewritten indexer reducer accumulates the scheduled microbatches per rank, so under any packing scheduler — dynamic CP in particular, where scheduled ≠ nominal is the norm — the logged `indexer loss` and `indexer raw loss` are scaled by scheduled/nominal. Training is unaffected. Since this PR rewrites the indexer normalisation and edits the lines on both sides of this one, it is the natural place to fix it:
